reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: In best Christopher Lloyd style, a man arrives in a busy diner claiming to be from the future. He (Sam Rockwell) also claims that this is the umpteenth time he has been to the place, at the same time, trying to recruit some of the diners to join him on a quest to thwart the ultimate takeover of society by an AI whizzkid. Of course they think he’s a few bricks short of a load, but when he reveals his detonator a few take notice. He already knows whom he wants, and whom he doesn’t and so armed with a reluctant band of “volunteers” and, for the first time, “Susan” (Juno Temple) off they set on a series of adventures that must keep them out of the reaches of the police and get them into the home of the young boy. Rockwell leads this entertainingly, if at times a little over-exuberantly, and he gels well with a Temple who wouldn’t have looked out of place atop a wedding cake. As their quest takes more shape, so does the message it makes no bones about delivering, and for any still sceptical about the manner in which mankind is sleepwalking into an artificially crafted, managed and controlled existence, this serves as a sharply written and potently acerbic critique on just how easy we might be manipulated in the future by the input of one innocent and fully functional young brain and machines that can thereafter write their own rules - for themselves and for us, too. A final plaudit has to go to the unnervingly menacing Artie Wilkinson-Hunt whose sparing contribution at the denouement gives the butter-wouldn’t-melt look on his face a distinctly unpleasant aftertaste. It is a bit long, and occasionally it does lose it’s way as we whittle down the characters, video-game style, but it’s an innovative story that ought to ring alarm bells.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Highly entertaining and pressing
This movie has spectacular casting, top to bottom, a plot that keeps you engaged, memorable and likable characters that makes the tension work, great direction, and a look that feels dynamic and real enough, even when it isn't.

The message is poignant too, which is great, but even without it, this would be a grand movie. I highly recommend it.

reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: Some prognosticators these days are contending that humanity is headed for a plunge off the edge of a cliff from which there’s no return. Others have even said that we’re already past that point. Either way, it would seem we’re at a critical juncture, a turning point of potentially mammoth proportions. But can anything be done to save us? That’s the question posed in director Gore Verbinski’s latest offering, a wild, whacked out sci-fi satire about the unfolding collapse of mankind and the efforts of a seemingly crazed time traveler from the future (Sam Rockwell) to save humanity. This manic, eccentric protagonist unexpectedly shows up in a present day Los Angeles diner to recruit a team of combatants to help him battle an evil force that will set mankind on an irretrievably unalterable path going forward. The enemy is a nine-year-old computer whiz (Artie Wilkinson-Hunt) who’s about to unleash a malignant form of AI that will lock us into an existence where everyone is hopelessly locked into the distractions of cell phones, social media, virtual reality and fascist AI, a paradigm enforced by relentless attack drones. With the help of seven ordinary individuals (all of them diner patrons who either volunteer or are unwittingly conscripted), the man from the future sets out on his quest to vanquish the enemy before it’s too late – an undertaking that he has apparently unsuccessfully attempted many times before. And, as this bizarre adventure unfolds, viewers are clued in on the back stories of several of these warriors and how their experiences have contributed to the emerging scenario. This includes the recent histories of Mark (Michael Peña) and Janet (Zazie Beetz), high school teachers who are unwittingly (and hysterically) confronted by a zombie-like student body involuntarily controlled by their cell phones, a segment reminiscent of “The Night of the Living Dead” (1968); Susan (Juno Temple), a middle-aged single mother who loses her son (Riccardo Drayton) in a school shooting but who is stunned when he is miraculously brought back to life as a clone (of sorts); and Ingrid (Haley Lu Richardson), a child’s birthday party entertainer who falls in love with a pizza deliveryman (Tom Taylor) who unsuspectingly becomes obsessed with virtual reality. These seemingly unrelated story threads ultimately become intertwined with one another as the film’s unlikely hero seeks to save the day. But can he? If this all sounds highly unusual, you’d be right – this is handily one of the strangest releases I’ve seen in ages. But it’s also one of the funniest, most outrageous tales I’ve ever seen committed to film. Besides the bitingly cynical and immensely creative humor served up here, “Good Luck, Have Fun, Don’t Die” imparts a decidedly important cautionary tale about us and our unknowing surrender to technology that may well end up taking us places we don’t want to go. There’s also an inherently strong metaphysical streak running through the narrative, particularly when it comes to the nature of alternate timelines and probable realities, not unlike themes played out in “Everything Everywhere All at Once” (2022) (but better explored here). Admittedly, this offering is a little overlong (especially in the final act), but, considering everything this title gets right (excellent performances, great special effects, big laughs), that’s easily overlooked. And it’s a fairly safe bet that the frantic nature of the picture and some of its edgy content won’t appeal to everyone. But those looking for something truly fresh, different and over the top while providing much to ponder, this one is clearly right up your alley. Keep that in mind the next time you speculate about the future – or step into your neighborhood diner.

reviews.author: Martin Oaks
reviews.content:
**When peril feels like a punchline**

The film kicks off with a premise that is as chaotic as it is magnetic in a run-of-the-mill Los Angeles diner—a backdrop that fades into the background when a man armed with a detonator bursts in with an wild claim: he is a time traveler who has failed 116 times before, and this is his last shot at saving the world. His mission is to recruit a group of everyday patrons with no special skills to form a ragtag team whose sole purpose is to stop a rogue AI fueled by the darkest corners of social media.

Verbinski’s ("Pirates of the Caribbean," "Rango"...) visual strengths coexist with the flaws of an overwrought script. Yet, the director proves once again his mastery at choreographing high-octane action sequences and extracting magnetic charisma from his cast. This is especially true thanks to the remarkable chemistry between Sam Rockwell, Haley Lu Richardson, and Michael Peña, who successfully keep the story's comedic momentum alive. Furthermore, the satire on our current technological dependency feels timely and visually stimulating, turning the chaos into a fairly enjoyable piece of entertainment.

However, "Good Luck, Have Fun, Don't Die" stumbles by trying to wear too many hats at once, shifting abruptly between absurd comedy, dystopian sci-fi, and slight touches of horror (at times, even evoking the grotesque surrealism of Jean-Pierre Jeunet). This tonal clutter dilutes the emotional weight of the climax, making moments of genuine peril feel like a mere punchline. In the end, while the premise relies on a rather conventional and predictable 'unlikely heroes' blueprint, the movie is entertaining and fast-paced, though perhaps too scattered for those of us who expected a social critique with a bit more bite.

reviews.author: Kingson S
reviews.content: An interesting premise and a very scary mind bending movie. Though it contains a lot of logic defying elements, the scary premise on how far AI would go is overwhelming me. The movie explores new aspects of AI implication not seen in other AI-based movies before.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A mysterious man from the future gathers a quirky group of diner patrons to thwart a rogue AI and save humanity.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In a bustling LA diner, a man claiming to be from the future appears with an urgent mission: to recruit a specific group of disgruntled individuals. Their task is to embark on a perilous one-night quest to prevent a rogue artificial intelligence from causing global catastrophe. This unlikely team must set aside their personal issues and work together to save the world, blending science fiction, action, and humor.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: The narrative unfolds in a quintessential Los Angeles diner, where a diverse array of patrons are each grappling with their own personal struggles and disappointments. Suddenly, a enigmatic figure, identifying himself as a 'Man from the Future,' makes a dramatic entrance, immediately disrupting the mundane evening. He reveals a grave truth: humanity is on the brink of destruction due to a rogue artificial intelligence that threatens to achieve terminal dominance. The Man from the Future explains that he has traveled back in time with a precise objective: to assemble a very particular team from the diner's occupants. These individuals, despite their apparent ordinariness or disgruntlement, possess a unique combination of skills, experiences, or even quirks that are crucial to his unprecedented mission. He informs them that they must join him on a one-night quest, an urgent and perilous endeavor to locate and neutralize the rogue AI before its apocalyptic plans come to fruition. The group, initially skeptical and reluctant, must overcome their disbelief and personal differences to unite against this existential threat. Their journey will be a blend of high-stakes action, unexpected comedic moments, and profound dramatic challenges as they fight for the fate of the world.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: The story centers on an extraordinary night at a typical Los Angeles diner, where various patrons are preoccupied with their everyday woes and personal frustrations. Their routines are shattered by the sudden arrival of a mysterious individual who claims to be a 'Man from the Future.' He delivers a chilling warning: a highly advanced, rogue artificial intelligence is on the verge of initiating a global catastrophe, threatening the very existence of humanity. To avert this impending doom, the man has traveled through time with a specific mission: to recruit a carefully chosen group of individuals present in the diner. He believes that this seemingly random assortment of disgruntled patrons possesses the unique combination of attributes necessary to succeed in his urgent quest. The newly formed, reluctant team must embark on a whirlwind one-night mission, putting aside their individual issues and disbelief to confront the rogue AI. Their adventure is portrayed as a genre-blending ride, incorporating elements of science fiction, pulse-pounding action, situational comedy, and human drama, as they race against time to save the world.

story_structure.climax: The surviving group breaches the hidden location where the core artificial intelligence is being created. In a tense, surreal confrontation combining physical and virtual environments, key team members must overcome personal traumas and physical limitations to install a critical safety protocol before the deadline expires.
story_structure.conflict: The patrons are initially deeply skeptical and hesitant to trust a self-proclaimed time traveler. However, as surreal technological hazards and escalating dangers disrupt the diner, the reluctant group is forced to unite and flee, committing to a high-stakes, single-night mission to avert the impending singularity.
story_structure.resolution: With the immediate threat addressed, the survivors process the immediate aftermath of their ordeal. However, the nature of the time-loop quest reveals deeper layers to the mission, setting up new parameters and hope for humanity's ongoing struggle against artificial intelligence.
story_structure.introduction: A disheveled 'Man from the Future' bursts into a Los Angeles diner, announcing that humanity faces an apocalyptic threat from an emerging artificial intelligence. He asserts that a specific combination of patrons present in the diner holds the key to stopping the AI before it gains sentience.
story_structure.risingAction: The team journeys through a city rapidly descending into chaos, facing bizarre algorithmic traps, techno-influenced hostiles, and unexpected personal revelations. As they navigate these surreal obstacles, individual members step up to use their unique quirks and skills to overcome each life-threatening hurdle, drawing closer to the AI's origin point.
